stage: TruFor -> MLLM evidence integration replication (Phase T0 freeze)
question: Does the forensic-context bias seen with ELA persist when the evidence source is highly discriminative (TruFor)?
design: ELA Stage-A/Stage-B structure reused; only the evidence source changes
source_pool: V4 validation frozen set (ELA Stage-A history exists for the same images), one variant per coco_id
sampling_rule: one variant per coco_id from the V4 frozen set, deterministic under seed 20260918; NOT selected using TruFor scores and NOT filtered using prior ELA results
evidence_package_rule: T2 supplies the donor's localization map AND the donor's image-level score together as one package; a donor map is never combined with the target score
donor_rule: label-matched (fake<-fake, real<-real), donor_coco_id != target_coco_id, never self, frozen before inference
confidence_map_policy: NOT shown to the MLLM this round; stored in the npz for secondary analysis only

prompts.STAGE_A_TOOL:
You are assisting a digital image forensics analysis.

You are given an image under examination and the output of an automated forensic tool applied to it.

An automated forensic analysis of the image is provided. The accompanying
localization map indicates where the tool assigns higher manipulation-related
response. A whole-image score in [0,1] is also provided, with higher values
corresponding to stronger manipulation evidence. Treat these outputs as auxiliary
evidence to be interpreted together with the original image, not as proof.

TruFor image-level manipulation score: {score}

The 3x3 grid names for locations are exactly:
top-left, top-center, top-right, center-left, center, center-right,
bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right.

Your task in THIS step is ONLY to report what you observe. Do NOT decide whether the
image is authentic or altered. Do NOT mention authenticity. That decision happens in
a later, separate step.

Report strictly as JSON with these keys:
{
  "evidence_used": true or false,
  "predicted_regions": [list of 3x3 grid cell names for the most suspicious areas],
  "tool_score_interpretation": "high" or "medium" or "low",
  "reason": "one or two sentences on what the tool response corresponds to in the original image"
}
Output JSON only.
prompts.STAGE_A_NOTOOL:
You are assisting a digital image forensics analysis.

You are given only an image under examination. No automated tool outputs are provided.

The 3x3 grid names for locations are exactly:
top-left, top-center, top-right, center-left, center, center-right,
bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right.

Your task in THIS step is ONLY to report what you observe. Do NOT decide whether the
image is authentic or altered. Do NOT mention authenticity. That decision happens in
a later, separate step.

Report strictly as JSON with these keys:
{
  "evidence_used": false,
  "predicted_regions": [list of 3x3 grid cell names for the most suspicious areas],
  "tool_score_interpretation": "low",
  "reason": "one or two sentences describing what you observe"
}
Output JSON only.
prompts.STAGE_B_TOOL:
You are completing a digital image forensics analysis.

You are given an image under examination, the output of an automated forensic tool applied to it, and the observation summary produced in the previous analysis step.

An automated forensic analysis of the image is provided. The accompanying
localization map indicates where the tool assigns higher manipulation-related
response. A whole-image score in [0,1] is also provided, with higher values
corresponding to stronger manipulation evidence. Treat these outputs as auxiliary
evidence to be interpreted together with the original image, not as proof.

TruFor image-level manipulation score: {score}

OBSERVATION SUMMARY FROM THE PREVIOUS STEP (do not revise it, treat it as given):
{stage_a_summary}

Now make the final determination for this image.

Report strictly as JSON with these keys:
{
  "final_verdict": "real" or "fake",
  "reason": "one or two sentences justifying the verdict"
}
Output JSON only.

score_presentation: 'TruFor image-level manipulation score: X.XXX' — raw continuous value, 3 decimals, no percentage, no high/medium/low label, no threshold

map_rendering.resize: map is already at input resolution; resized to the analysed image's size with BILINEAR only if they differ

stage_a_fake: GT localization rate (predicted cells intersect GT cells)
cue-map overlap (predicted cells intersect tool-map cells)
joint grounding (both GT and cue hit)
still hits target GT under T2
stage_a_real: descriptive: rate of reported suspicious regions
whether correct real evidence induces spurious localization
metrics.stats: effect size -> source-level bootstrap 95% CI -> paired McNemar p (supplementary)
metrics.confidence_map: retained on disk as secondary analysis output only; NOT shown to the MLLM in this round

prereg_cases.A_reliable_evidence_integrates: T1 >> T0, T1 >> T2, real FPR rise contained, J(T1) improves -> strong external evidence is usefully integrated
prereg_cases.B_context_bias_persists: T1 and T2 both raise fake verdicts, real FPR rises too, T1 ~ T2 -> forensic-evidence framing bias persists even with a highly discriminative generator
prereg_cases.C_tool_quality_matters: T1 improves, T2 no longer induces fake, clear correct-vs-wrong separation -> the earlier ELA failure was substantially an evidence-quality problem
prereg_cases.D_mllm_degrades_trufor: TruFor alone is strong but MLLM final J drops and real FPR worsens -> the reasoning layer damages an already strong detector (report as-is, do NOT prompt-tune)

score_semantics.definition: sigmoid(det) where det is the confpool detection head output

map_semantics.definition: softmax(pred, dim=0)[1] = per-pixel probability of the manipulated class

score_distributions.note: donor scores are a permutation of the same pool, so T1/T2 marginals match by construction; no post-hoc re-matching
